evidence: pyproject.toml:10 requires-python = ">=3.11"; asyncio.timeout was added in 3.11, so it exists on every supported version. sql_threads.py:155-163 wraps `await slot.acquire()` in `async with asyncio.timeout(WORKER_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S)` and catches bare TimeoutError. From my knowledge of CPython 3.11/3.12 asyncio/timeouts.py (not re-read here), Timeout.__aexit__ converts CancelledError to TimeoutError only when its state is EXPIRING and task.uncancel() <= the cancelling count recorded at entry. An external cancel() raises that count, so CancelledError propagates unchanged. On 3.11+ asyncio.TimeoutError is the builtin TimeoutError, so the except clause catches it. The code matches the claim.

Read CPython 3.11.16 asyncio/tasks.py wait_for (lines 473-479): on CancelledError while awaiting the waiter, `if fut.done(): return fut.result()` returns the result and swallows the cancellation. wait_for wraps slot.acquire() in a task; if that task acquired the slot (granted by release()) in the same tick the outer task is cancelled, fut.done() is true and wait_for returns True, so the cancelled caller proceeds to run the query. Input traced: waiter future resolved by slot.release() and outer task cancelled in the same tick. Versus locks.py Semaphore.acquire (3.11, lines 385-394): the cancellation is thrown at `await fut`; since fut was resolved (not cancelled), the handler does `self._value += 1; self._wake_up_next(); raise`, giving the slot back and waking the next waiter, and CancelledError propagates. asyncio.timeout (sql_threads.py:156-157) does not swallow cancellation, only converts its own timeout to TimeoutError. So the comment is accurate and the code form avoids the problem. The rejection line concerns the MySQL docstring, a different subject; graded without it.

Read Semaphore.acquire in CPython 3.11.16 (locks.py:364-398) and 3.12.13 (locks.py:363-397); they are identical. A granted waiter has had _wake_up_next do _value -= 1 and fut.set_result(True). A cancel in the same tick finds fut done, so Task.cancel cannot cancel it and sets _must_cancel. CancelledError is then thrown at `await fut`. The except branch sees `not fut.cancelled()`, so it does `self._value += 1; self._wake_up_next()` and re-raises. The slot is returned, so locked() is False afterwards when no other waiter exists. In sql_threads.py:156-157 the CancelledError leaves `async with asyncio.timeout` before line 169, so nothing is submitted. If the timeout caused the cancel, it becomes TimeoutError and then SqlWorkersBusyError (158-163), and still nothing is submitted. The rejection line concerns the MySQL runner docstring and does not touch this claim.
